paragraphs.title: The Dream and the Four Beasts

easy.explanation: Daniel saw four great beasts rising from the sea.
easy.q: What did Daniel see in his dream?

easy.explanation: The four beasts came up from the great sea.
easy.q: From where did the four beasts come?

easy.explanation: The fourth beast had ten horns.
easy.q: How many horns did the fourth beast have at first?

answers: It had eyes like a man and a mouth speaking great things
medium.explanation: The little horn had humanlike eyes and a mouth that spoke great things.
medium.q: What was unusual about the little horn?

medium.explanation: The leopard had four wings and four heads.
medium.q: Which beast had four heads and four wings?

medium.explanation: The four winds of heaven strove upon the great sea.
medium.q: What did the four winds of heaven do upon the great sea?

answers: Its wings were plucked, and it stood like a man
challenge.explanation: Its wings were plucked, it was lifted up, and it stood on human feet with a man's heart.
challenge.q: What change happened to the first beast?

answers: It did not rise from the sea
It was different, dreadful, and exceedingly strong
challenge.explanation: The fourth beast was different from all the others, dreadful, and exceedingly strong.
challenge.q: What distinguished the fourth beast from the beasts before it?

answers: A little horn arose and three were plucked up
challenge.explanation: Another little horn arose, before which three of the first horns were plucked up.
challenge.q: What happened among the ten horns?

paragraphs.title: The Ancient of Days and the Humanlike Figure

easy.explanation: The Ancient of Days sat upon the throne.
easy.q: Who sat upon the throne in the vision?

easy.explanation: His throne was like the fiery flame, and its wheels were burning fire.
easy.q: What was the throne like?

easy.explanation: The judgment was set, and the books were opened.
easy.q: What was opened when the judgment was set?

medium.explanation: His garment was white as snow, and his hair was like pure wool.
medium.q: How was the clothing of the Ancient of Days described?

answers: It was slain and its body was given to the burning flame
medium.explanation: The beast was slain, its body was destroyed, and it was given to the burning flame.
medium.q: What happened to the beast after the horn spoke great words?

medium.explanation: Thousands of thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him.
medium.q: How many ministered before the Ancient of Days?

challenge.explanation: He was given dominion, glory, and a kingdom.
challenge.q: What was given to the one like the Son of man?

answers: It belonged only to the fourth beast
It was everlasting and would not be destroyed
challenge.explanation: His dominion was everlasting, and his kingdom would not be destroyed.
challenge.q: What characterized the kingdom given to the humanlike figure?

answers: Thrones, the Ancient of Days, judgment, and opened books
The sea, four beasts, horns, and sleep
A kingdom, a bear, wings, and fire
challenge.explanation: The vision presents the thrones, the Ancient of Days, the judgment, and the opened books.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the heavenly court?

paragraphs.title: Daniel Seeks the Meaning of the Vision

easy.explanation: Daniel was grieved in his spirit, and the visions troubled him.
easy.q: How did Daniel feel after the vision?

answers: One of those who stood by
easy.explanation: Daniel came near to one of them that stood by and asked for the meaning.
easy.q: Whom did Daniel approach to understand the vision?

easy.explanation: The four beasts represented four kings who would arise from the earth.
easy.q: What did the four beasts represent?

answers: That he give him a kingdom
That he tell him the truth and interpretation
medium.explanation: Daniel asked for the truth and the interpretation of the things.
medium.q: What did Daniel ask the one who stood by?

answers: The saints would take and possess the kingdom
medium.explanation: The saints of the Most High would take and possess the kingdom forever.
medium.q: What would happen in the end according to the interpretation?

medium.explanation: An interpretation is an explanation of the meaning of something.
medium.q: What does the word “interpretation” mean in this passage?

answers: Daniel asked for the meaning, and the attendant told him
Daniel asked for a kingdom, and the attendant refused
Daniel asked to flee, and the attendant stopped him
challenge.explanation: Daniel asked for the meaning, and the attendant explained the beasts.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between Daniel's request and the attendant's response?

answers: The kingdom ultimately passes to the saints
There is no change in rule
challenge.explanation: The vision moves from the rule of the beasts to the saints possessing the kingdom.
challenge.q: What is emphasized in the movement from the beasts to the saints?

answers: The vision concerns kingdoms and their end
The vision concerns only the weather
challenge.explanation: The interpretation connects the beasts with kings and ends with the kingdom of the saints.
challenge.q: What general conclusion comes from the interpretation?

paragraphs.title: The Fourth Beast and the Horn

easy.explanation: Daniel wanted to know the truth about the fourth beast.
easy.q: About which beast did Daniel ask for special understanding?

easy.explanation: The horn made war with the saints.
easy.q: With whom did the horn make war?

easy.explanation: The Ancient of Days came, and judgment was given to the saints.
easy.q: Who gave judgment in favor of the saints?

answers: It was different, dreadful, and stronger than the others
It was the only beast without teeth
It did not rise from the sea
medium.explanation: The fourth beast was different from all the others and exceedingly dreadful.
medium.q: Why was Daniel especially interested in the fourth beast?

answers: It made war with the saints and prevailed against them
It gave the saints a kingdom
medium.explanation: The horn made war with the saints and prevailed against them for a time.
medium.q: What did the horn do before the Ancient of Days came?

medium.explanation: To stamp something with the feet is to trample or crush it.
medium.q: What does “stamped the residue with his feet” mean?

answers: Its power is temporary and not final
It has no power at all
challenge.explanation: The horn prevails for a time, but judgment comes and the saints receive the kingdom.
challenge.q: What does the sequence of events teach about the horn's power?

answers: The horn prevails for a time, but the saints possess the kingdom at last
The beast is weak, and the saints disappear
The Ancient of Days loses the judgment
challenge.explanation: The vision contrasts the horn's temporary success with the saints' final victory.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in the vision?

answers: The horns are connected with kings and the speaking horn
The horns have no connection with the vision
The horns belong only to the lion
challenge.explanation: The interpretation identifies the horns with kings and gives special importance to the little horn.
challenge.q: Why does Daniel ask about the horns as well as the beast?

paragraphs.title: The Interpretation of the Fourth Kingdom and Its Kings

easy.explanation: The fourth beast represented the fourth kingdom upon earth.
easy.q: What did the fourth beast represent?

easy.explanation: The ten horns were ten kings who would arise from the kingdom.
easy.q: What did the ten horns represent?

easy.explanation: The other king would subdue three kings.
easy.q: What would the other king do to three kings?

answers: It would devour, tread down, and break the whole earth
It would build up the earth
medium.explanation: The fourth kingdom would devour the whole earth, tread it down, and break it in pieces.
medium.q: How would the fourth kingdom act?

answers: He would be different and speak against the Most High
He would be the first among them
He would not rule at all
medium.explanation: He would be diverse from the first and speak great words against the Most High.
medium.q: How would the other king differ from the kings before him?

medium.explanation: He would think to change times and laws.
medium.q: What would the other king try to change?

answers: The other king rises after the ten kings
The other king is one of the four beasts
The other king rises before all the kings
challenge.explanation: Another king would rise after the ten kings and would be different from them.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the ten horns and the other king?

answers: He uses power to establish a different rule
challenge.explanation: Subduing three kings emphasizes his authority and his difference from the others.
challenge.q: What does subduing three kings reveal about the other king?

answers: The fourth kingdom, ten kings, and another king
Another king, four beasts, and ten books
The saints, a bear, and three rivers
challenge.explanation: The interpretation presents the kingdom, then ten kings, and afterward another king.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the development of rule?

answers: It will be taken away and destroyed
It will be given to the beast
easy.explanation: The judgment will take away his dominion and destroy it unto the end.
easy.q: What will happen to the wicked king's rule?

answers: The people of the saints of the Most High
easy.explanation: The kingdom will be given to the people of the saints of the Most High.
easy.q: To whom will the kingdom be given after judgment?

easy.explanation: The kingdom is described as an everlasting kingdom.
easy.q: How is the kingdom given to the saints described?

medium.explanation: First the king's dominion is taken away; afterward the kingdom is given to the saints.
medium.q: What comes first in the vision: the removal of the king's dominion or the giving of the kingdom to the saints?

answers: They will serve and obey it
medium.explanation: All dominions shall serve and obey the everlasting kingdom.
medium.q: What will the other dominions do concerning the everlasting kingdom?

medium.explanation: To take away his dominion means to remove his authority to rule.
medium.q: What does “take away his dominion” mean?

answers: The wicked rule is temporary, but the saints' kingdom is everlasting
The two kingdoms last the same amount of time
The saints give up the kingdom
challenge.explanation: The wicked king is destroyed, while the kingdom of the saints is everlasting.
challenge.q: What is the central principle in the change from the wicked king to the saints?

answers: All dominions under heaven will serve and obey it
Only one king will obey it
No one will know about it
challenge.explanation: The passage says that all dominions shall serve and obey the everlasting kingdom.
challenge.q: How is the extent of the everlasting kingdom emphasized?

answers: Judgment removes the opposing rule and gives the kingdom to the saints
challenge.explanation: Judgment ends the wicked rule and brings the giving of the kingdom to the saints.
challenge.q: What is the connection between judgment and the everlasting kingdom?

paragraphs.title: The End of the Vision and Its Preservation

easy.explanation: Daniel said that his cogitations greatly troubled him.
easy.q: How did Daniel feel at the end of the vision?

easy.explanation: Daniel's countenance changed in him.
easy.q: What happened to Daniel's countenance?

easy.explanation: Daniel kept the matter in his heart.
easy.q: Where did Daniel keep the matter?

medium.explanation: His troubled thoughts and changed countenance show that the vision deeply affected him.
medium.q: What does the change in Daniel's countenance show?

answers: He kept the matter in his heart
He gave it to a beast
medium.explanation: Although troubled, Daniel kept the matter in his heart.
medium.q: What did Daniel do despite his trouble?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that Daniel retained and treasured the matter within himself.
medium.q: What does “I kept the matter in my heart” mean?

answers: Daniel is troubled, yet he keeps the matter
Daniel is joyful and forgets the matter
Daniel is angry and destroys the vision
challenge.explanation: Daniel is troubled by the vision, but he does not reject it; he keeps it in his heart.
challenge.q: What contrast appears at the end of the chapter?

answers: It shows that the vision was important and deeply disturbing to Daniel
challenge.explanation: Daniel's troubled thoughts and changed countenance reflect the power of the vision.
challenge.q: How does the ending relate to the whole vision?

answers: He considered it important and did not disregard it
He replaced it with another dream
challenge.explanation: Keeping the matter in his heart emphasizes its importance and seriousness to Daniel.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Daniel's keeping the matter in his heart?
